sources.title: GLInt: Geometry-Matched Hard Negatives for Late-Interaction Retrieval
sources.snippet: I started with a narrow question: Do hard negatives mined by a multi-vector retriever produce a better late-interaction model than negatives mined by a dense retriever? Pffftt, Obviously! I introduce GLInt, which reaches 57.43 mean nDCG@10 on the 15 BEIR Tasks, starting from the unsupervised LateOn checkpoint.
